description.narrative: The development objective of the Social Safety Net Project for Cameroon is to support the establishment of a basic national safety net system including piloting targeted cash transfers and public works programs for the poorest and most vulnerable people in participating areas within the Recipient?s territory. The project has three components. The first is laying the foundations of a safety net system and supporting project management (US$7.8 million). This component has following two sub-components: (1) help the Borrower to develop systems to coordinate and manage safety nets programs for the poor and vulnerable; and (2) finance the cost of the management, coordination, and monitoring and evaluation (M and E) activities under this and the other two project components. The second component is the pilot cash transfer program with accompanying measures to boost household productivity (US$36.3 million). This component is for supporting the development and to boost the productivity of chronically poor households and serve as the cornerstone of Cameroon?s social safety net. Accompanying measures are to be developed to maximize the impact of the cash transfers on the welfare and productivity of beneficiary households. The third component is the public works program pilot (US$5.9 million). This component is for developing and piloting a labor-intensive public works program aimed to help vulnerable households deal with exogenous shocks (such as droughts or floods). The public works activities are to be coordinated with the cash transfer program so as to facilitate its implementation and reinforce its effectiveness.

The project development objective (PDO) is to support the establishment of a basic national safety net system including piloting targeted cash transfers and public works programs for the poorest and most vulnerable people in participating areas within the Recipient's territory.

title.narrative: Number of new community assets created or existing assets maintained

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded with 479 new community assets created or existing assets maintained, against an end target of 315.  </p>

title.narrative: Development and implementation of a functional and effective MIS system for the cash transfer and public works programs

comment.narrative: <p>The target was achieved with an MIS for both the cash transfer and public works program developed during the initial stages of the project. This existing MIS was subsequently upgraded for integrated management of the ordinary cash transfer program, emergency cash transfer program, public works program, procurement, accounting, and monitoring and evaluation.</p>

title.narrative: Development and implementation of an effective targeting mechanism for cash transfer programs

comment.narrative: <p>The target was achieved with an effective targeting mechanism established for both the cash transfers and emergency cash transfers, which incorporated elements of geographic, community and poverty targeting.</p>

title.narrative: Beneficiary households of regular cash transfers who have adopted essential family practices

comment.narrative: <p>It is not feasible to determine whether the end target for this indicator has been achieved, given it had not been measured at project completion.</p>

title.narrative: The per capita consumption level of households benefitting from cash transfers

comment.narrative: <p>No data was collected on per capita consumption effects.</p>

title.narrative: Beneficiary households of regular cash transfers participating in accompanying measures

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded with 100% of beneficiary households of regular cash transfers having participated in the accompanying measures, against an end target of 80%. There were challenges in delivering the accompanying measures to those in the North-West region due to the security situation, but these were eventually overcome.</p>
<p>The target was exceeded with 1,169,099 total beneficiaries for the cash transfers and public works program, against an end target of 834,000.</p>

title.narrative: Frequency of publication of monitoring reports

comment.narrative: <p>The target was partially achieved with a total of 16 monitoring reports having been produced over 9 years against an end target of one monitoring report having been produced every 6 months, or 18 reports over 9 years.</p>

title.narrative: Program management expenses as share of total program

comment.narrative: <p>The target was achieved with 18.17% of the total program budget going towards program management expenses, against an end target of 20%.</p>
<p>The target was exceeded with 3,683,412 effective days worked on the public works program, against a revised end target of 3,180,000 days.</p>
<p>The target was not met with only 45.56% of LIPW workers receiving their payment in a timely manner, against an end target of 80%.</p>
<p>The target was exceeded with 60,500 total direct beneficiaries of LIPWs, against an end target of 53,000.</p>

title.narrative: Timely payments of emergency cash transfers

comment.narrative: <p>The target was partially met with 70.19% of payments for the emergency cash transfers made in a timely manner, against an end target of 80%.</p>

title.narrative: Households benefitting from regular cash transfer program

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded with 85,000 household benefiting from regular cash transfers, against an end target of 82,000.</p>

title.narrative: Timely payments of regular cash transfers

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded with 86.8% of beneficiaries receiving their cash transfers on time, against an end target of 80%. The PIU had the capacity to ensure that all regular transfers were delivered on time. However, the delays observed for some payments were related to: (i) the baseline survey being carried out in some municipalities before the first payment; (ii) the security situation that emerged in the North-West; and (iii) the difficulties in replenishing the designated account for payment due to suspension of advances at the country portfolio level.</p>

title.narrative: The share of beneficiary households (of both cash transfer and public works program) who live below the poverty line

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded with 93.3% of beneficiaries selected for the CT and public works program living below the poverty line, against an end target of  70%.</p>

title.narrative: Creation and implementation of a permanent safety net institution within the Government

comment.narrative: <p>While progress was made against this objective, the target was only partially achieved. There are two institutions affiliated with the project at the central level, which includes the Social Protection Steering Committee and the PIU. The Steering Committee, which consists of representatives of key ministries and is headed by the Secretary General of MINEPAT, is responsible for all activities related to the implementation of a safety net system. The PIU has been extended beyond the life of this project with additional funds from the Government and the World Bank financing. The Government has also developed a social protection strategy that incorporates safety nets and allocated its own funds to expand the coverage of the project. </p>

title.narrative: Cash transfer payment system developed and implemented

comment.narrative: <p>The target was met with a cash transfer payment system being developed and implemented under the project, which facilitated the payment of regular and emergency cash transfers throughout the implementation of the project.</p>

title.narrative: Monitoring and evaluation system developed and implemented

comment.narrative: <p>The target was met with a functional monitoring and evaluation system having been developed for the project. It involved field teams (regional coordinators, focal points, field operators, etc.). Methods and tools to collect monitoring data were developed and tested. Field teams produced monthly reports on all project activities in their areas. Several evaluations (qualitative and quantitative) were designed and implemented. Regular quarterly reports were produced.</p>
